title: Lessons from Creath, then Chicago in 1920 with Wycliffe and Keppard
summary: Creath shows him passages on trumpet; in 1920 he goes to Chicago, reads first trumpet with Everett Robbins and Wycliffe's band beside Freddie Keppard, learning the New Orleans style.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Learning your horn: teachers, lessons and fees

blocks.x: I don't exactly, I can't recall the name of his boats, but anyhow, he got Willie Grant to work on his boat. Well, meanwhile, going back to Charlie that year after I worked at 19, when Charlie, to finish that season out, Charlie would have me to come down there every night, and then he would show me passages on his horn. Well, that's how I knew the trumpet might be in the sources like that, so it didn't take me long to catch the pencil on his horn. Then when the season was over in 1920, I came up there in Chicago. Yeah. I went there working with Everett Robbins, who was working with John L. Wycliffe. Oh yes, I've heard of that. Well, Wycliffe had Freddie Keppert playing with him. Well, since I was the best reader, they always put me on first trumpet, and put the weaker guys on playing another. And that way, I got to know to play right with the New Orleans filmers, and learned their style, because I was playing first and they were playing second.
